name: Aramanik
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Retired code, merged into Aasax [aas]; extinct via shift to Nandi; only lexical-recollection and language-shift papers found, no stress description

sources.citation: Kruijsdijk, Iris. 2024. The position of Asá and Qwadza within Cushitic. In Y. Huang, N. H. Kaldhol, J. J. Lim, S. Rose & A. Struthers-Young (eds.), ACAL in SoCAL: Selected papers from the 53rd Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 347-365. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.11210466
sources.note: Nothing: sec. 3.1 'Phonological evidence' is segmental sound correspondences only (Asá d ~ West Rift/Qwadza tl; š ~ ts); no occurrence of stress/accent/tone/pitch anywhere in the chapter. States all Asá data (334 lexemes) are taken from Ehret 1980, which adapted Winter 1979's field data from the last speakers/rememberers.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2014. Change Request Number 2014-042: adopted merge [aam] Aramanik into [aas] Aasax (effective 2015-01-12). SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Identity only: 'The original Aramanik language was a Cushitic language (or a non-Nilotic language with heavy Cushitic overlay) usually called Aasax (Fleming 1969) and is already included in a separate Aasax [aas] entry.'

sources.citation: Global Lexicostatistical Database (Starostin et al.), Aasax annotated 110-item wordlist (sources: Ehret 1980; Maguire 1928; Fleming 1969 cited in notes).
sources.note: Nothing; item-level source notes only, no prosodic remarks, forms cited without tone/stress marks.

sources.citation: Petrollino, Sara & Maarten Mous. 2010. Recollecting words and expressions in Aasá, a dead language in Tanzania. Anthropological Linguistics 52(2): 206-216.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Most recent primary data (2008 rememberers) by Cushitic specialists; short but may characterise the pitch/accent pattern of remembered words and compare with Winter's transcription.

sources.citation: Sommer, Gabriele. 1992. A survey on language death in Africa, Asa entry pp. 309-310. In Brenzinger (ed.), Language Death: Factual and Theoretical Explorations with Special Reference to East Africa, 301-413. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Summarises the state of documentation of Asa and lists sources; would confirm whether any phonological description beyond wordlists exists.

sources.citation: Ehret, Christopher. 1980. The Historical Reconstruction of Southern Cushitic Phonology and Vocabulary (Kölner Beiträge zur Afrikanistik 5). Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. (Asa material passim, vocabulary pp. ~279-388; discussion of Winter's Asa transcription.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Comparative phonology that explicitly discusses how Winter's Asa transcription was normalised and treats Southern Cushitic tone/stress; may state whether Asa forms carried marked accent and where.

sources.citation: Winter, Jürgen Christoph. 1979. Language shift among the Aasáx, a hunter-gatherer tribe in Tanzania: an historical and sociolinguistic case-study. Sprache und Geschichte in Afrika (SUGIA) 1: 175-204. Hamburg: Buske.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only substantial first-hand field record of Aasáx (last speakers, 1970s); Ehret 1980 says Winter's data were in 'extremely detailed phonetic transcription', and the accented autonym Aasáx implies prosody was marked -- the likeliest place for any remark on accent/tone placement.

sources.citation: Fleming, Harold C. 1969. Asa and Aramanik: Cushitic hunters in Masai-Land. Ethnology 8(1): 1-36.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The article that identified Aramanik with Asa and compiled the Merker/Maguire/own lexical data; may include transcription notes on accent.

sources.citation: Maguire, R. A. J. 1928. Il-Torobo. Journal of the African Society 27: 127-141, 249-268 (repr. 1948, Tanganyika Notes and Records 25: 1-27), with Aramanik and Mósiro vocabularies.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only lexical specimens recorded under the name Aramanik itself; colonial wordlists occasionally note where 'the accent' falls. 1928 volume is now US public domain, so a HathiTrust/JSTOR full view may exist.

sources.citation: Kießling, Roland (Southern Cushitic chapter) in Vossen & Dimmendaal (eds.) 2020, The Oxford Handbook of African Languages.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.access_detail: digital copy exists; only the abstract or an excerpt is open
sources.note: Google Books snippet: 'accent, only marginally distinctive, was largely predictable by phonotactic criteria' -- but the same snippet says that for lack of documentation of Aasáx the chapter restricts Southern Cushitic to West Rift, so the accent remark is NOT about Aasáx/Aramanik.
